newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Axa to launch US$125 mln China fund.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Axa to launch US$125 mln China fund.

text.p: French insurer Axa SA and two of its financial services subsidiaries will launch a US$125 million Chinese direct-investment fund this year, one of the subsidiaries, National Mutual Funds Management Ltd (NMFM), said.

Australia-based NMFM said that it, the Axa Group and Axa's U.S.-based investment banking arm, Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, would provide all the initial capital for AXA National Mutual China Number One Fund.
The fund is expected to swell to US$500 million within a few years as institutional and retail funds are drawn in, NMFM said.

The fund will be managed by DLJ and will invest 75 percent of its capital in joint-venture commercial enterprises in China, taking mostly minority equity stakes worth up to US$10 million each, NMFM said.

"They will be businesses that are very tied to the economic growth rates of China -- the consumer industries and basic-materials industries," NMFM marketing executive director Clinton Starr told a news conference in Melbourne.
The balance of the fund will be invested throughout the rest of Asia, excluding Japan, NMFM said in a statement.
The fund will be set up in the final quarter of calendar 1996 and "begin investing shortly thereafter", it added.
"The focus of the fund will be to try to co-invest with other Chinese and Asian and indeed Western investors," NMFM managing director Sam Kavourakis told the news conference.
The fund will be expected to yield a return of at least 20 percent over the longer term due to the relatively higher risk profile of the investments, he added.
"This type of investment does carry some greater risk ... but it also provides opportunities for very attractive investment returns," Kavourakis said.
NMFM is the funds management arm of National Mutual Holdings Ltd, owned 51 percent by Axa and due to list on the Australian and New Zealand stock exchanges next month.
National Mutual is lobbying for a licence to operate as a life insurer in China.
"It (the fund) certainly signals that Axa and National Mutual are long-term players in the Asian region and, perhaps more significantly, in China," Kavourakis said.
The fund will not invest in infrastructure or property, but these could be targeted later through the creation of a number-two China fund, he added.
"We are leaving our options open, but it's quite likely there will be a number-two fund and the funds could be co-invested," Kavourakis said.
